subtype: Approach: avoiding the data until forced [Pitfall]
passage:
I sit two desks from Hafsa in a shared office, so I see the Monday routine. The dashboard tab stays shut. Hafsa opens a design tool, refills the water bottle, answers messages. Once I joked, "Have you looked at the numbers?" and got a bright "Later!" I felt uneasy but didn't push.
This month a letter from the bank arrived. Hafsa read it standing up, sat down slowly, and finally opened the dashboard. I glimpsed a line sloping down for four months. Hafsa said only, "Okay," and cancelled the planned hire. I can't say whether it was fear or plain exhaustion I was watching.
By evening there was one cheaper plan left on the notepad.
— Nandini

qa.q: How long had the line on the dashboard been sloping down?
qa.a: It had been sloping down for four months.

qa.q: What might Hafsa have been feeling each Monday while keeping the dashboard tab shut?
qa.a: Probably dread about the numbers, though Nandini cannot be sure: the closed tab and the bright "Later!" suggest Hafsa was steering away from something painful.

qa.q: What could Hafsa have done differently on those Mondays?
qa.a: Hafsa could have looked at the numbers for a few minutes each week with someone supportive, so a slow slide would show up while there were still several options.

qa.q: What is it like for Nandini to watch a desk neighbour avoid the numbers?
qa.a: Nandini feels uneasy and unsure, wanting to say more but not wanting to push, so the joke was as far as it went.

grounding: The account shows a founder skipping the dashboard weekly until the bank forces a look, by which time the decline is long and choices are fewer.
